title: At the Jazz Band Ball and the Delivery Stable Blues lawsuit
summary: Brief talk of the tune he wrote with Shields and the injunction over Delivery Stable Blues.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right. Now, speaking of jazz bands, Nick, let me interrupt you. Didn't you write a tune called At the Jazz Band Ball? That's right. Well, we...

That's right. That's Larry Shields, who, of course... Harry Shields, rather. The clarinet player. And we have a recording of it now by the original Dixieland jazz band at the jazz band ball. 楽 The End The End The End The End Fine. And that was at the jazz band Ball. Now to get back to our interview with world famous Nick LaRocca, the daddy of jazz. Nick, for the next record we have selected, which will be coming up in a moment or two, we have Delivery Stable Blues. Now, that's a very interesting name. Was there a story connected with this at all?

Well, there was a story connected with it. There was a litigation. One of the men in the early Chicago bands that I had let go, he wanted a piece of it, which I thought he wasn't entitled to, because the tunes were mine.
And he had some publisher to go on to work and put it out, and I had taken an injunction and stopped him.

Mm-hmm. Now, may I ask you this? Uh, you were able to prove, of course, in court that you had composed the Liver Stable Blues, because I noticed that the copyright is in your name. That's right. Now, let me ask you this. In your composition, how did you manage to write the music? Because...
